navigationSource.warning: Archive includes changes later than3.58f. Bounded assembly below corroborates the selected rules in the original3.58f binary.

analysis: New evidence is ordinary address-bounded LLVM objdump and PE byte/reference inspection, not newly returned REA dossiers or original execution. Hopper could not launch its local bridge (Connection is invalid); its retained180 evidence was exported, but cleanup acknowledgement was unavailable. No reinstall, external binary upload or Windows execution was attempted.

observations.fact: UN:K applies to the independent32-bit week suppression and message-index fields.
M0/M1/M2/M3 select normal/none/forced creature/plague. M2 separately applies the creature operand.
K1 changes the normal week selector so the random creature branch cannot be taken.
K2 resolves a z-index1..500 and formats its current contents before replacing the final week notification pointer.
The month overrides return normal, forced-double or plague selection and the chosen creature pointer.

implementation: Map-local K1 suppression, K2 live message reference/reset and M0..3 selection, replicated and saved in the existing source state.
The existing native Inferno Grail effect keeps priority, as required by the primary UN documentation. Existing native week/month growth and plague arithmetic are used.
Forced calendar selection still consumes the ordinary native calendar roll; no Windows/native random-sequence equivalence is claimed.
Creature IDs use the already installed original source bindings, not an assumed numeric native index.
limitations: Only solo source initialization is established by these native calendar controls. A preliminary private hotseat fixture exposed a source-initialization dialog on the other local interface; this multi-human source-host path remains unvalidated. Ordinary Goonk hotseat regression tests pass and original campaigns are single-player.
The forced-double native stock proof uses original source creature0/Pikeman; this control does not independently exercise every possible creature ID.
Calendar parity does not establish an original scenario quest, combat or victory. Campaigns remain disabled.
